Discovery's push.expo false (an own server whose operator has not agreed) → no registration, said plainly.

Owners, admins and editors answer and approve; viewers read only (roleCan from src/auth/role.ts). The redact-question switch is owner and admin only (W2 US-014b: workspace:manage); everyone else sees its state.

Lock screen: Open and Answer on an unlocked phone. A question can be answered from the notification (Reply…, unlock required); approvals and Review tickets only open the app, so the output is seen first. A social post is never approved from a notification.
Inside the app, Face ID (passcode as the fallback) before approve or answer: a setting, on by default, client-side only; the settings copy says it is checked on this phone only. No server step-up.

A question push carries its text and options; every other push is generic; a per-workspace switch redacts questions (then Open only). Android lock-screen visibility PRIVATE. The app never rewrites, re-titles or re-presents a notification (no local notification), so the server's title badge (PRD-264 D17) is what the person sees.

A self-hosted server pushes through Expo only after its operator agreed (discovery push.expo). When it is false the phone registers nothing and the Notifications screen says so in plain words. Gerard's standing decision: Expo 'enhanced push security' stays off on the Automatos EAS project.

Three push types: Needs an answer (question_pending, approval_pending, mission_plan_ready), Ready for review (review_pending), Auto messaged you (auto_message, which also carries the daily digest). Everything else stays in the in-app inbox.

The daily digest is Auto's message in the person's Auto thread at 07:00, 08:00 or 09:00 in the phone's time zone; every day, with a per-person switch, on by default (W2 K12, the lead's default for PRD-266 open question 3).

The app verifies sig (signature v2, KP6) with the device's push_key, and that it is fresh, before acting on any notification action; on a mismatch, a v1 or unknown version, or an iat outside the window it posts nothing and opens the app.

Writes (answer, approve, a preference change) are never queued offline or retried in the background; the server's compare-and-swap answer is the truth. Question text, replies and payloads are never persisted, logged, breadcrumbed or sent to Sentry: no log line or breadcrumb carries a notification's title, body, question, options or sig (logs carry kinds and counts; nothing in src/push or src/step-up imports @sentry/react-native).
The app deletes nothing: 'Remove this phone' revokes only this phone's own device row; no account or workspace deletion anywhere.
No pointer to creating an account anywhere: no 'Create an account', 'Sign up' or 'No account?' link, button or copy (gate-enforced on the wave's added copy).

No copy says 'nothing leaves your server' or anything as broad (never leaves, no data is sent, 100% local, fully private, stays entirely on your …): even paired to a self-hosted install, push goes through Expo and Apple or Google once the operator agrees. The push copy names Expo's push service where it matters and makes no claim about where other data goes (gate-enforced).
Nothing about plans, credits or prices.

The AI label rules stay: src/styles/ai-label.tsx is never edited or restyled; this wave adds no composer (so it mounts no AiLabel); the push title's AI badge is the server's and the app never strips it (no scheduleNotificationAsync, no re-presented copy).

A W2 contract that differs from these notes is read from the code and the DONE mark says what changed. W1's committed device routes are read, not assumed.

Signature v2 (lead, 21 Oct; W2 K9 word for word): sig = lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, key = push_key as UTF-8, message = the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical JSON array ["v2", type, workspace_id, notification_id, grant_id, link_type, link_id, ticket_number, question, options, iat] serialized as Python json.dumps(fields, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False), which equals JavaScript's JSON.stringify(fields) byte for byte (measured 21 Oct on every published case: quotes, a newline, accented and astral characters, integers). The order is fixed; a string field the payload omits is ""; options is the payload's list in order, or []; iat is the payload's integer (epoch seconds, stamped when W2 builds the message). The payload is {v: 2, type (the push type: needs_answer | review | auto_message), workspace_id, notification_id?, grant_id?, link_type?, link_id?, ticket_number?, question?, options?, iat, sig}, every id and ticket_number a JSON string. The signature covers every field but sig itself, so the workspace, the notification id, the link and the ticket number are authentic. The phone refuses — treats as unverified: nothing actionable — a v other than 2 (v1 included), a field of the wrong JSON type, and an iat more than PUSH_SIG_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (604800, 7 days) old or more than PUSH_SIG_MAX_FUTURE_SECONDS (300) ahead of the phone's clock. ONE shared vector file, owned by W2 (orchestrator/tests/fixtures/prd266_push_signature_vectors.json, schema 'automatos-push-signature-vectors/v2'), copied byte for byte (US-015a). The app still acts only in its current workspace (a push for another workspace's device row is not this session's) and still checks a signed link for staleness (KP9), not for forgery.

Categories: automatos.question.0, .1, .2 and .3 each offer 'Reply…' (text input, isAuthenticationRequired, opens the app) and 'Open'; automatos.open offers 'Open'. NO option buttons: iOS and Android draw a category's buttons with the titles the app registered beforehand (expo-notifications setNotificationCategoryAsync), and W2 shares one category per option count, so one question's option texts cannot be its buttons without a Notification Content or Service Extension — a native target and a new build (open question). Options are answered in the app: Open lands on the question. EVERY action opens the app (opensAppToForeground true): expo-notifications 0.32.17's iOS EmitterModule calls the response's completionHandler right after emitting it (ios/EXNotifications/Notifications/Emitter/EmitterModule.swift), so a background answer can be suspended mid-request; foreground, the app verifies, posts once and shows the honest result. No Approve action anywhere (D18, D45).

decisions.text: POST /api/v1/approval-grants/{grant_id}/answer answers {grant} and does not say whether the agent resumed (the HTTP path ignores apply_question_answer's AnswerOutcome), and a compare-and-swap loser still gets 200 with the winning grant. So: 200 with status 'granted' and the answer_text this phone sent → 'Answered #N.' (or 'Answered.'); 200 with another answer, or 422 'not open' → 'That question was already answered.'; never 'resuming' or 'resumed' until the route reports it (open question; A3's 'Answered — the agent is resuming.' overclaims today).

link_type → screen through the foundation's builders: question → cc.questions (no per-question route: FOUNDATION GAP), task → cc.ticket(id), social_post → cc.social(id) (KP17), chat → chat(id), approval_grant, mission and anything else → home (the needs strip; the phone has no approvals or Missions screen and Studio's governance pane is a web page, D3). Each is re-checked first (pending questions, GET the ticket, the post, the chat); gone → a plain notice and a fallback; a network failure or a 403 → the target screen, which shows its own state. An unverified push follows no link: home with the unverified notice.

A phone registers (POST /api/v1/mobile/devices: install_id, platform, app_version, locale, timezone, expo_push_token, and name — the phone's model name, which W2 US-009 stores so Studio's Phones & devices shows it) only when the server has the 'push' capability and push.expo, the build has an EAS projectId and the OS permission is granted; again when the token, locale, time zone, app version, name, workspace or server changes, or after 24 h. The returned push_key is saved before registration counts as done. A null push_key with no stored key for that device: hosted → revoke own row and register again (W1 re-mints after the person's own revoke), at most once a day; own server → 'key_missing' (no re-key route exists for an active paired row: open question; a self-revoke would end the device token). OS permission switched off → PATCH push_enabled false once; on again → register (W2 US-009 turns push back on). 409s become plain statuses and are never retried in a loop. The install id is the connect kit's, never a second one.

Never asked at launch or on mount. Asked only from a person's tap: the in-context sheet (offered once the status is 'ask' and something waits for the person — the needs-you total above zero — or from the second session on; at most twice, a week apart) or the Settings button. Android: channels exist before the request (Android 13 shows the prompt only then).
decisions.source: PRD-001 §4.8 ('after the first useful moment, never at launch'), kit

decisions.text: PUT /api/notification-preferences replaces ALL of the caller's rows for each event_type it names (bulk_update_preferences; W2 US-014a's contract), so a switch sends every row GET returned for each event of its push type, every destination and channel_connection_id kept, only the 'push' rows changed, a missing push row added. The type → events map is GET's push_types (W2 US-014a), else the named fallback PUSH_TYPE_EVENTS. The digest switch is the 'daily_digest' push row; the digest time is THIS phone's device row (PATCH digest_time).

Gated in the app: answer (option or own words), approve a ticket, approve a Mission plan, grant a tool, approve a social post. Not gated: reject, deny, withdraw, dismiss, send back, request changes, report. A phone with no passcode or biometrics passes with a Settings note. Turning the setting OFF needs a pass first. A notification Reply is not gated (D18: the unlocked phone is the check).

The app icon badge is the server's needs-you total (FND-5's useNeedsYou), set while the app runs and 0 after sign-out; the server's pushes carry no badge (W2's PushMessage has none), so the number refreshes when the app runs.

While the app is open: an unverified push shows nothing; a verified one shows its banner and list entry (sound for questions only), the banner suppressed when the person is already on its target; a verified push invalidates the needsYou and questions families. The handler's verification has a 2 s budget; a timeout counts as unverified.

A hosted phone with a device row shows 'Remove this phone' on Account: DELETE its own row, clear the push state on the phone, stay signed in; notifications stay off until 'Turn on notifications' (W1 re-enrols a row its own person revoked). Sign out also revokes the row first (W2 US-009), with the still-valid Clerk token, then clears and signs out. An own server keeps the connect kit's 'Remove this phone and forget this server' (one button, never two).

An approval_pending push about a social post opens that post as it will publish (cc.social(id)), where Approve (exact version, Face ID) and Request changes live; the notification itself offers Open only (D45: never approved from a notification). The A3 kit's 'No entry from a notification' meant no push wiring in A3: this wave owns the entry (open question to confirm).

The push record (server origin, workspace, device id, push_key, Expo token, fingerprint) is ONE expo-secure-store item, keychainAccessible AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY (readable for actions after the first unlock; never in a backup or on another phone), under a key declared in the app's ONE secure-storage key registry (src/lib/secure-keys.ts, started by the foundation's US-005a token cache, whose index lists every key the app writes): the connect kit's reinstall wipe (US-006c) and sign-out clear every registered key, so a reinstalled phone starts with no push key. Sign-out and Forget this server unregister the device (its row revoked on the server) and delete the key. Never in MMKV, the query cache, a log, a toast or Sentry. MMKV holds only non-secret switches and counters (Face ID setting, prompt declines, handled response keys).
decisions.source: kit (connect KC9 pattern), lead (release audit, 20 Oct)

decisions.text: No registerTaskAsync in v1: every action opens the app (KP7), and W2 sends no content-available pushes. expo-task-manager and UIBackgroundModes remote-notification stay installed for later.

Android channels 'questions' (Questions, HIGH), 'review' (Ready for review, DEFAULT) and 'auto' (Auto, DEFAULT), each lockscreenVisibility PRIVATE, ids equal to W2's channel_id. Android delivery through Expo needs FCM: android.googleServicesFile in app.json and FCM V1 credentials on the EAS project (native, not in the A0 build: open question); until then Android registers but receives nothing.

userStories.title: Push data layer: the route table, zod schemas for the push payload and every server answer, API functions over the foundation client, push query keys
userStories.description: As the push wave, I need typed calls for every endpoint the phone uses for push — W1's device routes, the preferences, W2's push settings, the answer and mark-read routes the notification actions use, and the stale checks — all through the foundation's client (D-ONE-CLIENT), and one zod schema for the payload every notification carries (KP5).

userStories.title: The signature check (v2): UTF-8 bytes, HMAC-SHA256 over the native SHA-256, the canonical message, the freshness window, a constant-time compare, and the ONE shared vector file
userStories.description: As a phone, I act on a notification only when its sig verifies with my push_key, because anyone holding my Expo push token can send me a push (PRD-266 §4.4, D-SIGNATURE, KP6). Pure TypeScript over an injected SHA-256, so vitest runs it in node; the device uses expo-crypto's digest.

userStories.title: Reading a notification: what expo-notifications hands over → a verified push or nothing actionable; the action → an intent; each response handled once
userStories.description: As the action handler, I need one pure place that turns a received notification or a response into an intent — open a screen, post an answer, or open the app with nothing done — so an unsigned or forged payload can never post anything (PRD-001 §4.8, D-SIGNATURE, KP6, KP7).
